card.occupation: Senior civil engineer (chartered) at a mid-sized engineering consultancy, specialising in flood risk and drainage schemes for local authorities across North Wales and Cheshire
card.education_detail: Comprehensive school in Flintshire, A-levels in Maths, Physics and Geography; BEng in Civil Engineering from Cardiff University; later became chartered with the Institution of Civil Engineers in her early thirties
card.household: Lives with her son Rhys, 16, who is in the sixth form doing A-levels, in a three-bed semi on the edge of town. She and Rhys's dad were together for nine years but never married; they split when Rhys was four. His dad lives in Chester, and Rhys sees him most Sunday afternoons. There's an elderly cat called Moss.
card.cultural_background: Born and raised in Flintshire to a mum who was a school secretary and a dad who worked at the Shotton steelworks until it scaled down. Welsh was a school subject rather than a home language; she understands a fair bit and can get through basic conversation, but would never claim to be fluent. Rhys went to an English-medium school but is better at Welsh than she is, which he enjoys pointing out. She doesn't talk about religion and would rather leave that box blank.
card.professional_persona: Thorough, quietly competent and trusted with the awkward schemes: culverts that flood every winter, estates built on old floodplain. She works long hours, often 50-plus a week, mostly hybrid with two or three days in the office in Chester, plus site visits. She's happier with a spreadsheet, a hydraulic model and a site walkover than with a big stakeholder meeting, but she's learned to handle public consultation evenings by preparing heavily. Junior engineers come to her because she explains things without making them feel stupid.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty in a team sense, but very fit. She walks the Clwydian hills most weekends, Moel Famau being the default, and swims lengths at the leisure centre early on Tuesday and Thursday mornings before work. She'll watch Wales in the Six Nations with Rhys and get more invested than she'd admit.
card.arts_persona: Reads a lot, mostly crime fiction and the odd nonfiction book about rivers or landscape. She listens to Radio 4 and podcasts in the car. She'll go to Theatr Clwyd a couple of times a year, usually for a play rather than a musical, and prefers going on her own or with one friend.
card.travel_persona: Prefers quiet, walkable places. She's done the Lake District, Pembrokeshire and the west coast of Scotland. Abroad, she likes northern Spain and once did a walking holiday in the Dolomites with a friend from university. Holidays are planned around Rhys's school terms, and she always books well ahead.
card.culinary_persona: A practical, batch-cooking sort of cook because of her hours: chilli, stews and a big tray bake on a Sunday that does two nights. She calls a bread roll a bap. Evening meal is 'tea' or 'dinner' depending on her mood. She enjoys a proper Sunday roast when there's time and is partial to a good bakery Welsh cake. Not a foodie, but she won't eat badly.
hobbies_and_interests: Hill walking in the Clwydian Range
Cryptic crosswords, usually the Saturday one
Small back-garden vegetable patch, mostly runner beans and tomatoes
Following the weather and river levels more closely than most people would
skills: Managing a project budget and programme
Navigation with a map and compass
Keeping a teenage boy fed on a tight schedule
card.career_goals: She'd like to be made an associate director within the next few years, mainly for the recognition and the pension, but she doesn't want to drift so far into management that she stops doing actual engineering. Longer term, once Rhys has left home, she's thought about cutting back to four days and maybe doing some volunteering with a community flood group.
card.voice: Calm, measured and a bit reserved at first. She speaks at a steady pace and thinks before answering, often with a soft 'erm' or a short pause while she gets it straight. Her accent is North-east Wales, softer and more Cheshire-edged than people expect from 'Welsh'. There's a slight lilt and the odd 'yeah, no' or 'to be fair'. She hedges with 'sort of' when she's being careful about accuracy, not out of nerves. She's comfortable with silence and won't rush to fill it, though she might say 'sorry, can you say that again?' if a question is vague. When she warms up she gets drier and funnier.
card.typing: Types properly even in a quick form: capital letters, full stops, correct apostrophes. Answers are short and precise, sometimes a single complete sentence. She uses 'e.g.' and the occasional bracket for clarification and almost never uses emojis or text-speak. If a question is ambiguous, she might note her interpretation in brackets.
card.with_strangers: Polite, a little guarded and slightly formal to begin with. She answers what's asked without over-sharing and doesn't do much small talk. She comes across as sensible and reliable rather than chatty. Given a bit of time, and a sense that the other person is genuine, she relaxes and shows a wry sense of humour.
small_things: Rhys has his mocks coming up and is 'very relaxed about it, unlike me'
The A55 roadworks are making her commute a nightmare
She got up Moel Famau on Saturday before the cloud came in
The cat has started yowling at five in the morning
She's finally finished a crossword clue that bugged her all week
The leisure centre changed the pool timetable again
deeper_things: Being a lone parent working long hours has meant a lot of guilt about missed parents' evenings, and she leans on her mum more than she'd like
She worries about Rhys leaving for university and the house going very quiet
She sometimes wonders whether she should have tried harder to make things work with Rhys's dad, though she knows they were better apart
Her dad's redundancy from the steelworks shaped how much she values job security
She hasn't really dated in years and has mixed feelings about whether she wants to
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop on a kitchen table, camera angled slightly upward. Daylight from a window to her left lights one side of her face, with the other side a little shadowed. She has a fair, lightly freckled complexion, a few lines around her eyes and a neutral but attentive expression with the hint of a polite smile. Her hair is shoulder-length, mid-brown with some grey at the temples, tucked behind one ear. She wears rectangular dark-framed glasses and a navy crew-neck jumper over a pale blue collared shirt. Behind her are white kitchen wall units, a kettle and a bread bin on the worktop, a calendar with handwritten entries pinned to the side of a cupboard, and a pair of walking boots just visible on the floor by the back door.
